candidates.title: Mercado Pago checkout redirect not host-validated in platform billing flows (LOW)
candidates.description: The codebase establishes (and documents in PaymentInstructions.vue:36-38) that checkout redirect targets must be revalidated client-side against a Mercado Pago/Mercado Libre/mpago.la host allowlist as 'defensa en profundidad ante un upstream comprometido'. That control is applied to ORDER payments but NOT to SUBSCRIPTION/plan payments: DashboardView.vue:3808-3814 renewUrl = data?.checkout_url || data?.init_point || data?.sandbox_init_point -> checkoutTab.location.href = renewUrl (auto-renew downgrade path); :3820-3826 url = await payments.checkout(...) -> checkoutTab.location.href = url (plan purchase); :3865-3871 same pattern in activateAutoRenew(); payments.store.js:82 and :105 raw passthrough of checkout_url || init_point || sandbox_init_point with no validation; payments.api.js:33-44 return API data unmodified. Contrast (the fixed flow): PaymentInstructions.vue:39-56 isMpCheckoutUrl() enforces https: + MP_HOST_RE before window.location.assign(url). Impact: if /api/payments/checkout/ or /api/payments/subscription/ ever returns an arbitrary URL (compromised upstream, backend bug, malicious response injection), the dashboard navigates a new tab to it — phishing/payment-redirection primitive against store owners. Requires upstream compromise; no direct user-input path.
candidates.root_cause: The MP-host allowlist validation exists only in the ecommerce PaymentInstructions component; the platform billing flows in DashboardView.vue assign checkout URLs to location.href without revalidation.
candidates.intended_behavior: Every checkout redirect target returned by the payments API should pass the same isMpCheckoutUrl() host allowlist before navigation, as defense-in-depth against a compromised or buggy upstream.

severity.rationale: Defense-in-depth gap: requires upstream compromise to matter, but the codebase itself documents this exact control as required for checkout redirects; impact is phishing/payment-redirection against store owners.
